# Tagcast 1.6.0 — Split albums with a reviewed selection

## Separate albums that ended up together

Choose **More album actions → Split album…**, select the tracks to move, and
enter the new album's title, release year and disc number. Review both the
selection and the tracks remaining before confirming the change in iBroadcast.

- Optional upload-group suggestions use different upload days, known years and
  restarting track numbers. They help select possible editions; nothing is
  preselected or split automatically, and a year difference alone is not enough.
- Track IDs, titles, numbers, years, performers, credits, genres and artwork stay
  unchanged. Playlists keep the same tracks. The new album's primary artist is
  copied from the original album; its year and disc number are your choice.
- Tagcast checks the original membership before writing and reads back both
  albums afterwards. The queue and playback remain independent.
- Creation and movement are separate operations. Unconfirmed results are never
  automatically retried; reload and check both albums before making more changes.
  A partial move or an empty album may remain after a failure. There is no Undo.

Current limits: one native source disc at a time, 2–500 active tracks, with at
least one track left behind. **Combine Multi-Disc Album Sets** must be off.
Albums with additional album-artist credits are blocked until those credits can
be preserved reliably on creation. The original album's rating and local
favourite are not transferred. Existing local music files are never modified.

The illustrated [Split albums guide](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/wiki/Split-albums)
shows the successfully tested *Comment ça Va* example: thirteen 1983 tracks and
eleven 1991 tracks separated into two albums.

## A clearer empty Now playing workspace

With an empty queue, Now playing now shows a simple explanation and **Browse
albums**. Empty lyrics panels and inactive queue actions are hidden. The normal
workspace returns as soon as tracks are queued. New controls and messages are
translated into English, Dutch, German, French, Spanish and Japanese.

## Downloads and compatibility

Standalone downloads are included for macOS Apple Silicon, macOS Intel, Windows
x64 and Linux x64, each with a SHA-256 companion. The macOS downloads are
**Developer ID signed and notarized by Apple**; signatures, stapled tickets,
Gatekeeper and extracted application startup are checked before publication.
Windows Authenticode signing through SignPath is not active yet.

Quit the older app before upgrading. Settings and sign-in data are preserved.
Linux still requires a graphical desktop and compatible libraries; Ubuntu
24.04's sandbox policy can need distribution-specific setup. Keep Chromium's
sandbox enabled. Python/browser use and the bundled `tagcast-cli` remain available.

Experimental Gapless Playback remains optional and disabled by default.
Unsupported transitions use normal playback; universal sample accuracy across
formats and platforms is not claimed. This release does not change the audio engine.

The illustrated [PDF manual](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/wiki/PDF-manual)
remains the labelled 1.4.0 edition; the Wiki documents newer features.

**Code signing policy:** macOS is Developer ID signed and notarized. SignPath
Foundation support for Windows remains pending; these Windows downloads are
unsigned. [Signing details](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast#code-signing-policy)
and [privacy policy](https://github.com/cyberdeliaAI/tagcast/blob/v1.6.0/PRIVACY.md).
